The present petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No.481/2022 under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) registered at Police Station Rajouri Garden on the ground of settlement.
Later, offences under Sections 376/377 of the IPC were added.

sentences.text: 4. The petitioner no.1 is the husband of the respondent no.2 and the petitioner no.2 is the father of the petitioner no.1.
The marriage of the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 was solemnized on 7th July, 2021 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies.
5. Dispute arose between the petitioners and the respondent no.2, which resulted in filing of the present FIR by the respondent no.2 against the petitioners.

6. Now the parties have settled all their disputes in terms of Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)
dated 28th June, 2023, which has been filed as Annexure P-2 to the petition.
The parties have also been granted divorce by mutual consent vide decree dated 21st July, 2023.

7. As per the MoU, various items such as jewelry and Streedhan etc. have been returned to the respondent no.2 and a Demand Draft of Rs.4,50,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no.2 in Court today.
8. Issue Notice.
9. Notice is accepted by the learned ASC, appearing on behalf of the State and the counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent no.2.
10. Learned ASC opposes the present petition on the ground of the seriousness of the charges.

11. I have heard the parties and perused the material on record.
12.
The respondent no.2 is present in Court and has been identified by her counsel as well as by the Investigating Officer (IO).
She informs the Court that she has settled the matter of her own free will and without any coercion.
She further states that she has no objection to quashing of the FIR.
She has also filed A No Objection Affidavit, attesting the same.
13. The petitioners are also present in Court and have been identified by This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/12/2023 at 22:33:13 their counsel.
They affirm the statement of the respondent no.2 and undertake to abide by the terms of settlement arrived at between the parties.
14. The Court is conscious that cases relating to offences under Section 376 of the IPC should not normally be quashed on the ground of settlement.
However, it is an admitted position that the present FIR emerges out of a matrimonial dispute and that the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 were married at the time of filing of the present FIR.
Therefore, taking into account the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the aforementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
